newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African court awards bail to convicted rightist.
newsitem.headline: S.African court awards bail to convicted rightist.

text.p: White rightist leader Eugene Terre'Blanche was convicted on Wednesday of trying to murder one black employee and assaulting another.

But the defiant leader of the Afrikaner Resistance Movement (AWB), who walked out of the court as the judge read the conviction, returned after a lunch adjournment and was allowed to leave on 1,000 rand ($225) bail.
His case was postponed to June 17 when he will hear his sentence.

He was found guilty of attempting to murder former employee Paul Motshabi, 27, who suffered severe brain damage in a beating in March last year. He was also convicted of serious assault on another black man, named as John Thembeni Ndzima, last November.
Both men were employees in a security firm run by Terre'Blanche.
"The accused is found guilty on both charges," magistrate Chris Eksteen ruled in his judgment.

But immediately after the magistrate spoke, Terre'Blanche jumped from his seat in the dock and told Eksteen: "May God watch over you for what you have said. It will echo in the homes of every Boer (Afrikaner)".
Fighting back tears, Terre'Blanche added: "You have become the accomplice of the (ruling) African National Congress...You are a traitor...the judgment is a political judgment."
As his followers applauded and cheered, Terre'Blanche walked out, telling reporters outside the courtroom in Potchefstroom west of Johannesburg: "Today the war has started."
Magistrate Chris Eksteen did not attempt to stop the right-wing leader and did not finish reading his ruling. His written judgment was subsequently entered into the court records.
When the court sitting resumed, Eksteen told Terre'Blanche: "The court cannot turn a blind eye to the events that unfolded before lunch."
However, he made no order about the outburst.
Eksteen initially set bail at 2,000 rand but reduced it to 1,000 rand when a weeping Terre'Blanche said he could not afford the higher bail and gave assurances he would not abscond.
Bail was not opposed by the prosecution and after the amount was set, AWB supporters in the courtroom came up with the money within minutes.
The courtroom was jammed with black onlookers standing against the walls while white AWB members, most in camouflage clothes, packed the seats.
Tight security was evident with at least 15 policemen in the courtroom. Outside, the street in front was closed to traffic by police and a police helicopter circled.
